game.name: Archons
game.short_description: Archons is a Roguelite/Survivor game where you control two characters, the Archons- simultaneously! Customize your build and abilities to fit your own unique playstyle and blast your way through enemy parasites and bosses!

placements.verbal_evidence: I think Arkin deserves a solid A spot.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Arkins is a horde-like (vampire survivors / bullet heaven) game where you control two characters at once, which he says he has never seen done before. He treats the single-player two-character setup as the more interesting way to play and calls it a pleasantly amazing surprise. The music-synced sound design and slow, forgiving onboarding win him over. The main complaints are the short length (three levels, repeated bosses) and that many abilities do nothing in single-boss fights. He places it in A tier.
praise: Two-character control is a unique twist on the horde-like genre and feels great once it clicks
Abilities tie into the two-character movement, so each run feels different
Everything is synced to the electronic music beat, and this can be used strategically (e.g. timed grenades)
Gentle progression: starts simple, introduces more, slow early gameplay lets players adjust to the controls
Good damage feedback and readability, so he usually knows why he took damage even with characters far apart
Solid meta progression and enemy design; attractive look and feel
criticism: Game is short: only three levels, each ending in a boss
Bosses are identical every run and the difficulty meter adds little new
Wants more content and enemy variation in levels
On-death and bounce-type abilities are useless against lone bosses with no adds, discouraging those boons
The two-character control may not click for everyone
unique_points: Controlling two characters at once in a horde-like is a novel mechanic combined with a fitting genre
Beat-synced damage ticks and ability triggers merge music and sound design, and enable rhythm-based strategy
Design lesson: give boss fights small adds so on-kill and bounce effects still trigger
commentary.quote: Arkin deserves a solid A spot.
design_criteria: Novelty/unique twist: two-character control is the core hook
Audio/music integration: beat-synced effects and sound design
Meta-progression: substantial unlocks that suit the learning curve
Onboarding and difficulty curve: slow, forgiving start that builds comfort
Content volume: only three levels and repeated bosses
Boss design and build synergy: lone bosses invalidate some ability types
Enemy design: liked, but wants more variety
Replayability: abilities plus movement make runs feel different

community.one_liner: A short roguelite/survivor bullet-hell from BulletHell Studios in which one player controls two characters at once, one per hand/stick, with weapons that fire in time to the music.
community.consensus_summary: Archons is a small, cheap indie (Steam, Windows only, Dec 6 2024) that sits at Very Positive on Steam (about 92-94% of roughly 430 reviews). Players love the two-character control hook, the tight positioning-focused combat and the music that syncs with weapon attacks. The recurring complaints are that it is short (around 3 hours for the main story, 3 bosses/levels), that content and enemy variety are thin, and that solo play is very mentally taxing while the game is clearly tuned for a controller or local co-op. It has no Metacritic or OpenCritic entry, so there is no critic consensus; reception is entirely player-driven. A few reviewers feel it is under-supported, and one said it seems abandoned, but I found no public patch notes confirming or refuting that. It is frequently discounted to about $1 (90% off the $9.99 base).
best_things: The dual-character mechanic is fresh: controlling two Archons at once is hectic but 'just works' and creates a flow state
Weapons and attack animations are synced to the soundtrack, praised as a standout (composer Oliver Orand is named in a review)
Movement and positioning matter more than spamming abilities; you cannot stand still or circle-strafe and win
Polished and respects your time: a short run-based experience, with endless mode and a hard mode for replay
Spectacular boss fights and satisfying build combos when rolls line up
Great value at its frequent steep discounts; StarCraft references delight some players
Full controller support and local split-screen co-op
worst_things: Very short: main story is only 3 stages/bosses, and reviewers call it short or a bit short
Limited enemy variety; reviewers say many enemies use the same attack pattern and there are few maps
Maps are too dark and hard to read; some players had to raise brightness
No camera control and a rotating camera that adds to the stress
Mouse and keyboard play is poor or problematic; a controller is strongly recommended
Weak ability synergies and lackluster ability evolutions; the Archon ultimate is a static barrage
Polish and optimization issues reported, plus poor translation and UI complaints in one negative review
Ultimate is hard-coded to F even after rebinding (one reviewer)
improvements: Add a real single-character or AI-companion mode so solo players are not forced to control two characters
More content: more bosses/stages, maps and enemy types with distinct attacks
Give abilities real synergies with the Archon ultimate and stronger ability evolutions
Improve map brightness/visibility and add camera options
Fix mouse and keyboard support, rebinding bugs (ultimate on F) and UI/translation rough spots
Add online co-op (requested in Steam discussions) and New Game+ / quality-of-life features
Differentiate the two characters visually (color suggestion in discussions)
unique_things: You control two characters simultaneously, one per hand, as a survivor-style bullet hell, compared by one reviewer to It Takes Two meets Furi
Attacks and weapons are rhythm-synced to the music
Bloodrunes let you sacrifice health for power, and there are multiple currencies to spend
Local split-screen co-op where each player pilots one Archon, versus solo where one player pilots both
Positioning-first design rather than screen-filling particle chaos or auto-fire snowballing
tedious_or_disliked: Solo play demands a lot of mental juice and is described as stressful; one reviewer called it the most stressful roguelike they had tried
Some unlocks/research feel grindy ('after a few grind sessions') and one reviewer said difficulty collapsed once a certain research was unlocked
Healing pickups are time-limited and released by breaking containers, so they get wasted when damage breaks them at random
Dark maps and lack of camera control are frustrating
Reported bugs: freezing after reroll, an ice-ground mechanic problem in Endless Hard mode, and an achievement (Heartache) not unlocking
divisive_points: Solo vs co-op: some say the game is meant to be played solo (that is the challenge), others say it is made for co-op and solo is too hectic
Price and length: some call it great only on discount while others say even full price is fair for the polish
Difficulty: challenging until the two-character skill clicks, then some find builds too easy or some weapons unviable on hard mode
community.reception_notes: Launched Dec 6 2024 on Steam for Windows only (no Mac/Linux listed, no console release found). Steam reviews have stayed Very Positive, with about 410-430 total and a recent-review score of 92%; it still gets positive reviews in 2026, including several by players who say they slept on it. Base price is $9.99 and it is heavily discounted to about $1 at times. Steam Community threads in early 2026 show the dev-facing asks (online co-op, mouse support, single-character mode) and some bug reports; one negative reviewer felt it was abandoned and lacked an Early Access tag, though I could not verify the update cadence from public patch notes. No professional critic reviews, Metacritic or OpenCritic pages were found; Deku Deals lists Metacritic as not yet available. Revenue and owner figures are third-party estimates (Boxleiter method), so treat them as order of magnitude only.
